To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) exercise induces a systemic metabolic state that protects against metabolic disease and cancer; 2) exercise protects against retinal degeneration; 3) exercise induces a metabolic state that promotes neurogenesis and protects against cognitive decline.
exercise-induced signals from skeletal muscle can protect against metabolic diseases, cancer, retina degeneration and memory decline.

exercise induces a coordinated crosstalk between the brain, liver and skeletal muscle that protects against metabolic disease, and that exercise-induced crosstalk between brain, skeletal muscle and adipose tissue protects against memory loss and retinal degeneration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and physiological mechanisms of exercise and the role of exercise in human health and disease
the role of exercise in health and disease and in particular with the role of the skeletal muscle as an endocrine organ.
understanding how the human body adapts to exercise and how this can be used to prevent or treat disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exercise is good for your health.
the exercise is good for health and that the health benefits of exercise are more than meets the eyes, but the molecular mechanisms are largely unknown.
exercise can be considered a form of medicine, and that exercise can be used to treat and prevent many diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
exercise can prevent and treat a variety of age-related diseases.

the exercise-induced metabolic adaptations that are associated with the protection against metabolic and cardiovascular disease, are not limited to the skeletal muscle but involve crosstalk with other tissues, such as the adipose tissue and liver.
exercise is good for you, but the mechanisms by which it is good for you are much more complicated than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the benefits of exercise are not limited to the exercising tissue.
exercise is more than just a way to burn calories.
exercise is more than meets the eyes, and that exercise-induced metabolic and hormonal signals can be beneficial to the brain, eye and other tissues.
